correctness.rationale: For fixed q, matching the copy with the first one and the copy with the last one gives q≤A≤2q and m−q≤C≤2(m−q). The unfilled before-one zeros of the second copy and after-one zeros of the first copy add to B, proving sufficiency. Requiring at least s+1 integers in the interval is equivalent to A,C≥2s and 2s+(A mod 2)+(C mod 2)≤B≤m−s. Subtracting 2s from every gap preserves outer parities and gives exactly the existence inequalities at m−3s, including empty ranges and m=0. Taking tail differences gives the census and extrema. Summing S(m) gives (1+x+x²)/(1−x)^3; taking the tail difference and summing in t gives the stated bivariate series. The limiting conditional tail follows from the quadratic leading term with t=floor(mu)+1; the conditional mean follows also by the incidence identity. A fresh exhaustive position-split check (/workspace/audit_replay_1.py) found identical root sets for all 252 words at m=0 through 6; at m=6 there were 27,45,18,1 words with respectively 0,1,2,3 roots. The all-length result rests on the proof, not the bounded replay.
